short: Four election wins, a devaluation, and the referendum that kept Britain in Europe.
full:
Harold Wilson won four general elections and governed from 1964 to 1970 and again from 1974 to 1976. He promised the white heat of technological revolution and delivered comprehensive schooling and the Open University, alongside a run of liberalising measures passed under his home secretary Roy Jenkins: the abolition of capital punishment and of theatre censorship, the decriminalisation of homosexuality, and the legalisation of abortion.

Economic weakness dominated. He resisted devaluation for three years before cutting the pound from $2.80 to $2.40 in November 1967, insisting on television that the pound in your pocket had not been devalued. He kept British troops out of Vietnam despite American pressure, sent them into Northern Ireland in 1969, and on returning to office renegotiated Common Market terms and won the 1975 referendum by two to one. He announced his resignation in March 1976 and left office in April, shortly after turning sixty.
